patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with long-standing type 1 diabetes and Hashimoto hypothyroidism who joins in 2022. Alopecia areata is diagnosed by dermatology in 2024, she is admitted with DKA during a viral URI in February 2025, and in October 2025 she has idiopathic acute transverse myelitis with a good recovery through rehab and PT.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31 y/o woman, elementary school teacher, transferring care from her prior primary care office; wanted a practice where she can reach the doctor directly. Records requested.

Type 1 diabetes, long-standing. On Lantus 18 units at bedtime and Humalog with meals, counting carbs at 1 unit per 12 g with a correction scale. Checks fingersticks 4-5 times a day. No severe lows, no ED visits for sugars that she can recall. Last eye exam about a year ago, told no retinopathy.

Hashimoto hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 88 mcg, takes it first thing with water. Feels well on it.

PMH: as above. PSH: wisdom teeth out at 18.
Meds: insulin glargine 18 u qHS; insulin lispro per carb ratio 1:12 + correction; levothyroxine 88 mcg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother Hashimoto's. Father type 2 DM. Maternal aunt with RA. Sister has celiac disease.
SH: lives in Amherst with a roommate. Teaches 2nd grade. Never smoked. A drink once or twice a month. No drugs. Walks most evenings.

ROS: negative except as above. No polyuria, no numbness in the feet, no vision change.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, thyroid smooth, not enlarged, no nodules. No adenopathy. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no tenderness; injection sites in the abdomen without lipohypertrophy. Extremities no edema. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+ DP/PT, monofilament sensation intact bilaterally. Scalp and skin normal.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Type 1 diabetes: A1c, CMP, urine albumin/creatinine, lipids today. Continue current regimen. Eye exam due — she will book with her optometrist.
2. Hashimoto hypothyroidism: TSH today, continue 88 mcg.
3. Health maintenance: flu shot this fall at a nurse visit. Prior office records for Pap and vaccine history.
Return in 3 months for diabetes follow-up.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two things today.

1) Hair loss. About six weeks ago her hairdresser pointed out a bald spot at the back of her head; since then she's found two more. No itching, pain or burning. Hasn't changed products, no tight hairstyles, no recent illness. Not losing hair diffusely in the shower.
Exam: scalp with round, smooth, completely bald patches, no scale, no redness. Skin otherwise normal.
This looks like patchy alopecia, possibly alopecia areata, which would fit with her other autoimmune conditions. Thyroid has been steady. Referring to dermatology to confirm and talk about options. She'd like an appointment early in the summer break.

2) T1DM. Meter averages a bit better this spring. No lows needing help. A1c today.

Meds unchanged. Vitals as charted.

Plan: derm referral placed. A1c today. Physical in August.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
DERMATOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/01/2024
Referred by: primary care physician
Reason: patchy hair loss of the scalp

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for referring Ms. Hartley, a 32-year-old teacher, whom we saw today.

History: Over roughly three months she has developed several round bald patches on the scalp, each sharply outlined and completely smooth. They cause no pain, itching or burning. No new hair products or traction styles.

Past history: type 1 diabetes; Hashimoto hypothyroidism. Wisdom teeth extraction at 18.
Medications: insulin glargine 18 units at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals (carb ratio 1:12); levothyroxine 88 mcg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: mother with Hashimoto thyroiditis, father with type 2 diabetes, maternal aunt with rheumatoid arthritis, sister with celiac disease.
Social: never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks a month; elementary school teacher.

Examination: Three coin-sized patches of alopecia on the scalp with no scale and no erythema. Short broken exclamation-mark hairs at the edges of the patches. No palpable cervical or occipital nodes. Fingernails show pitting. No other skin lesions on full skin exam. Otherwise unremarkable.

Data: Your office's recent hemoglobin A1c was 6.8%. Today we drew TSH, CBC and ANA: TSH 2.5 mIU/L (reference 0.4-4.0), CBC within normal limits, ANA negative.

Impression: Alopecia areata, patchy, with nail pitting, in the setting of other autoimmune disease.

Plan: We reviewed the usual course and the treatment options, and agreed to start a potent topical steroid. Clobetasol propionate 0.05% solution: apply a thin layer to each bald patch twice daily; keep it off the face. We discussed skin thinning, which we will check for. Follow-up in 3 months.

Sincerely,
Dermatology

documents.title: Dermatology visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Christine, I got the dermatology letter. Alopecia areata confirmed, and the bloodwork they drew (thyroid, blood counts, ANA) was all normal. The clobetasol solution they started is a strong steroid, so use it only on the patches and keep it off your face. I've added both to your chart. Let me know if anything changes before your August physical.

documents.title: RE: Dermatology visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you! Honestly relieved it has a name. See you in August.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical. Turned 33 last month. Summer was restful. Using the clobetasol solution on the patches twice daily without irritation. Wearing her hair down over them and isn't bothered. Diabetes steady; no severe lows.

Medications: Lantus 18 units qHS, Humalog 1:12 + correction, levothyroxine 88 mcg, clobetasol 0.05% solution to scalp patches BID. NKDA.
Problems: T1DM, Hashimoto hypothyroidism, alopecia areata (derm 7/2024, on topical clobetasol).
Social: still teaching 2nd grade; never smoker; alcohol a couple of drinks a month.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. General well. Scalp: three smooth round bald patches, no thinning of the skin. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix normal; Pap/HPV collected. Skin otherwise clear. Feet: intact skin, pulses full, monofilament normal both feet.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- T1DM: A1c, CMP, urine albumin/creatinine, lipids. Continue regimen.
- Hypothyroidism: TSH.
- Alopecia areata: clobetasol per derm; derm recheck in October.
- Cervical screening: co-test today.
- Flu shot in the fall; she gets COVID boosters at the pharmacy.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pap test is normal and HPV is negative, so the next cervical screen is in five years. Your other labs from the physical were all fine as well — thyroid normal, kidneys and urine normal, cholesterol good. Have a great start to the school year.

documents.title: Dermatology Follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
DERMATOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 10/07/2024

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Hartley returned for her alopecia areata, three months after starting clobetasol propionate 0.05% solution twice daily to the patches. She has used it as directed and has had no irritation.

Examination: Fine new hairs growing in all three scalp patches. No new patches. No skin atrophy, telangiectasia or folliculitis at the treated sites. Nail pitting unchanged.

Impression: Patchy alopecia areata, responding to topical steroid.

Plan: Continue clobetasol 0.05% solution twice daily to the patches. Recheck in 3 months.

Sincerely,
Dermatology

Date of visit: 01/13/2025

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Hartley returned for her alopecia areata, six months into clobetasol propionate 0.05% solution twice daily to the patches.

Sincerely,

conditions.label: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis without coma

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PROVIDER NOTE
Date of service: 02/18/2025, arrival 21:40

CC: confusion, vomiting, fast breathing

HPI: 33-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, Hashimoto hypothyroidism and alopecia areata, brought in by her roommate, who found her confused and vomiting and breathing rapidly. Per patient and roommate, she has had a cold for several days — congestion, sore throat, cough — with poor appetite, and has not been taking her insulin regularly while sick.

Meds: insulin glargine 18 units nightly; insulin lispro with meals, carb ratio 1:12; levothyroxine 88 mcg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: ill-appearing, drowsy but answers questions. Mucous membranes dry. Deep, rapid respirations. Fruity odor on the breath. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. No focal neuro deficit.

Data: arterial blood gas with high anion gap metabolic acidosis, pH 7.14. Glucose 438, bicarbonate 9, anion gap 25, potassium 5.3. Beta-hydroxybutyrate 6.4. Urinalysis positive for ketones and glucose. SARS-CoV-2 PCR not detected.

ED course: two liters normal saline, insulin infusion per DKA protocol, potassium added to fluids once K below 5.

Impression: diabetic ketoacidosis precipitated by viral upper respiratory infection and missed insulin.
Disposition: admitted to the medical ICU.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 02/18/2025   Discharged: 02/21/2025
Admitting unit: medical ICU, transferred to medicine floor 02/19/2025

Principal diagnosis: diabetic ketoacidosis, type 1 diabetes
Secondary: viral upper respiratory infection; Hashimoto hypothyroidism; alopecia areata

Hospital course:
Presented from home after several days of a viral URI with irregular insulin use; confused, vomiting and tachypneic on arrival with dry mucosa, Kussmaul breathing and ketotic breath. Arterial gas showed a high anion gap metabolic acidosis (pH 7.14); glucose 438, bicarbonate 9, anion gap 25, K 5.3, beta-hydroxybutyrate 6.4; urine positive for ketones and glucose. Hemoglobin A1c 7.8%. COVID PCR negative.
Managed in the ICU with IV fluids, insulin infusion and potassium replacement. Mental status cleared within hours. Anion gap closed overnight and she was moved to the floor on 2/19, bridged to subcutaneous glargine and lispro at her home doses. Eating normally by 2/20. URI symptoms improving.
Diabetes education reviewed sick-day management: never stop basal insulin, check glucose every 2-4 hours and ketones when ill, fluids, and when to call or come in.

Condition at discharge: stable, alert, ambulatory.
Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications (unchanged):
- Insulin glargine 18 units subcutaneously at bedtime
- Insulin lispro with meals, 1 unit per 12 g carbohydrate plus correction
- Levothyroxine 88 mcg daily

Follow-up: primary care within one week.

conditions.label: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis without coma

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 4 days after discharge from a 3-day admission (ICU then floor) for DKA. Summary reviewed.

She says she felt so sick with the cold that she couldn't eat, and figured she shouldn't take insulin without eating — skipped the Lantus two nights and most of the Humalog. Her roommate found her confused on the 18th. She's embarrassed and wants to make sure it doesn't happen again.

Now: eating normally, energy coming back, cough nearly gone, no fever. Sugars since discharge 100s-180s. Taking Lantus 18 nightly and Humalog with meals.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, comfortable. Mucous membranes moist. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
1. DKA, resolved. Precipitant: viral URI with missed basal insulin. Went over sick-day rules again in detail — basal insulin always, even if not eating; glucose every 2-4 hours; ketone check if over 250 or vomiting; sugar-containing fluids if not eating; call us early, any hour, if ketones moderate/large or she can't keep fluids down. She has urine ketone strips at home. Wrote the plan out for her fridge.
2. URI — resolved.
3. T1DM — no dose changes. BMP today.
4. Hashimoto, alopecia areata — stable.
RTC May for routine DM visit, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Checking in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Back at school this week and feeling like myself again. Sugars have been behaving. The sick-day sheet is on my fridge. Also saw my bloodwork from last week was normal — thank you.

documents.title: RE: Checking in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: So glad to hear it. Yes, the chemistry panel was completely back to normal. Remember you can reach me directly if you ever get sick and the numbers start climbing.

Plan

documents.title: Head cold
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Morning — I picked up a cold from my class, stuffy nose and scratchy throat since Sunday. No fever. Sugars are running a bit higher (low 200s a couple of times) and I checked ketones twice, both negative. Took my Lantus as usual. Anything else I should be doing?

documents.title: RE: Head cold
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sounds like you're doing exactly the right things. Keep taking your Lantus every night, cover meals with Humalog plus correction, drink plenty, and recheck ketones if you're over 250 or feel nauseated. If ketones come back moderate or large, or you can't keep fluids down, call right away — day or night. Feel better!

documents.title: After-hours call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pt called my cell at 6:50. Two days of tingling that started in her toes and has crept up to around her belly button, legs getting weaker — had trouble with the stairs last night — and she's had trouble getting her urine started since yesterday. Sugars fine, no fever. No back trauma.

Concerned for a spinal cord process. Told her to go to the ED now, not to drive; her roommate will take her. Called ahead to the ED physician.

medications.sig: 1 g IV once daily for 5 days

reports.study: MRI thoracic spine with and without contrast
reports.text:
MRI THORACIC SPINE WITHOUT AND WITH IV GADOLINIUM
Indication: progressive bilateral leg weakness, ascending sensory change, urinary retention.
Technique: sagittal and axial T1, T2 and STIR images; post-contrast T1 sagittal and axial.
Findings: Ill-defined T2-hyperintense signal within the spinal cord extending from T5 to T7. No enhancement of the lesion after gadolinium. Vertebral body heights and alignment preserved; marrow signal normal. No disc herniation, canal stenosis or cord compression. No epidural collection. Paraspinal soft tissues normal.
reports.conclusion: T2-hyperintense intramedullary lesion from T5 to T7 without enhancement. No compressive lesion.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text:
MRI BRAIN WITHOUT AND WITH IV CONTRAST
Indication: transverse myelitis, evaluate for demyelinating disease.
Findings: No T2/FLAIR white matter lesions. No abnormal enhancement. No restricted diffusion. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. No mass, hemorrhage or extra-axial collection. Optic nerves symmetric and normal in signal. Major flow voids present.
reports.conclusion: Normal MRI of the brain. No demyelinating lesions.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PROVIDER NOTE — 10/29/2025, arrived 07:40; PCP called ahead.

Chief complaint: leg weakness and trouble urinating x 2 days.

HPI: 34-year-old woman with T1DM, Hashimoto hypothyroidism, alopecia areata and DKA in February of this year. Two days of worsening weakness in both legs. Tingling began in the toes and has risen to the level of the umbilicus. Since yesterday, difficulty starting her stream and incomplete emptying. Had a mild cold about three weeks ago that went away on its own; no other recent infections and no recent vaccines. No back pain, no trauma, no vision loss.

Meds: glargine 18 u nightly, lispro with meals (1:12), levothyroxine 88 mcg. NKDA.

Exam: alert, oriented, anxious. CN intact. Arms normal strength and reflexes. Legs: strength 3/5 bilaterally, reflexes brisk/hyperreflexic at knees and ankles, Babinski present bilaterally. Light touch and pinprick reduced below the umbilicus. Bladder scan post-void residual 520 mL; Foley placed.

Labs: WBC 7.0 (7,000/uL). ESR 20 mm/h. CRP 1 mg/L. CMP normal. Aquaporin-4 and MOG antibodies sent.
MRI thoracic spine: T2-hyperintense cord lesion from T5 to T7, no enhancement with gadolinium.

Impression: acute myelopathy, likely transverse myelitis. Neurology consulted at bedside; admitted to neurology for IV steroids and workup.

documents.title: Neurology Discharge Summary
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission 10/29/2025 — discharge to acute inpatient rehabilitation 11/04/2025

Diagnosis: idiopathic acute transverse myelitis, T5-T7

Presentation: 2 days of progressive bilateral leg weakness with an ascending sensory level to the umbilicus and urinary retention, three weeks after a self-limited respiratory illness. Leg strength 3/5 with hyperreflexia and bilateral Babinski signs. MRI: non-enhancing T2 lesion T5-T7.

Workup:
- MRI brain with and without contrast 10/30: normal; no demyelinating lesions.
- Lumbar puncture 10/30: CSF WBC 11/uL, lymphocyte predominant; protein 49 mg/dL; glucose 71 mg/dL; oligoclonal bands absent.
- Serum aquaporin-4 IgG negative; MOG IgG negative.
- WBC 7.0, ESR 20, CRP 1, CMP normal.

Treatment: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily x 5 days (10/29-11/2), completed; no oral taper. Glucose rose on steroids as expected and was covered with correction insulin in addition to her usual basal-bolus doses; back to home doses at discharge.
Bladder: Foley removed 11/2; voiding trial passed, post-void residuals under 100 mL since.

Status at transfer: strength 4-/5 in both legs, walking short distances with a walker and assistance. Sensation still reduced below the mid-abdomen, improving.

Discharge medications: insulin glargine 18 units at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals (1:12 plus correction); levothyroxine 88 mcg daily. Methylprednisolone course complete.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: inpatient rehabilitation; neurology clinic in about 6 weeks; repeat thoracic spine MRI in about 6 months.

documents.title: Inpatient Rehabilitation Discharge Summary
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
ACUTE INPATIENT REHABILITATION — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 11/04/2025 from neurology; discharged home 11/20/2025.

Rehab diagnosis: paraparesis due to idiopathic acute transverse myelitis (T5-T7), s/p IV methylprednisolone.
Other: type 1 diabetes on basal-bolus insulin; Hashimoto hypothyroidism; alopecia areata.

Course: 3 hours/day of PT and OT. Steady gains in strength and gait. Glucose managed on her home regimen with her own carb counting; no hypoglycemia requiring treatment by staff. Bladder: voiding independently throughout, no catheterization needed.

At discharge:
- Strength: hip flexors 4/5 bilaterally; knee extension, ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion 4+/5 bilaterally.
- Gait: about 150 feet with a rolling walker, supervision on stairs.
- Sensation: numbness of both feet persists; trunk sensation improved.
- Independent with self-care.

Equipment: rolling walker, shower chair.
Medications: insulin glargine 18 units at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals per carb ratio 1:12 plus correction; levothyroxine 88 mcg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Plan: outpatient PT twice weekly; PCP within 1 week; neurology follow-up as scheduled. Off work for now.

orders.reason: Gait and leg strength after transverse myelitis

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with her mother, walking in with the rolling walker. Home 4 days from inpatient rehab after a week on neurology for transverse myelitis (T5-T7). Neurology and rehab summaries reviewed in full.

She's tired but encouraged. Legs a little stronger every day; feet still numb, "like wearing thick socks." Bladder working normally — no retention, no incontinence. Bowels normal. Sugars were high during the steroid days but have settled to her usual range on the home doses; no lows. Sleeping ok. Scared at first, now focused on PT.

Meds: glargine 18 u qHS, lispro 1:12 + correction, levothyroxine 88 mcg. Steroid course finished 11/2. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, good spirits. Lungs clear, heart regular. Legs: hip flexion 4/5, distal 4+/5 bilaterally; decreased light touch both feet. Gait slow and steady with walker. Feet: skin intact, no wounds, pulses normal.

A/P
1. Idiopathic acute transverse myelitis, recovering. Outpatient PT referral placed (twice weekly). Neurology follow-up mid-December, repeat MRI in spring per neurology. Foot care with reduced sensation — daily inspection, well-fitting shoes.
2. T1DM: stable after steroid hyperglycemia. Continue. A1c due in February.
3. Hashimoto, alopecia areata: stable.
4. Flu vaccine today (deferred this fall during the illness).
5. Work: on leave through winter break; we'll do short-term disability paperwork.
RTC 6-8 weeks, sooner if any new weakness, numbness, vision change or bladder trouble.

documents.title: Disability paperwork
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Short-term disability claim form dropped off by pt's mother. Clinician section routed to PCP. Hospital and rehab summaries attached. Completed form faxed to the insurer 11/26; copy scanned to chart.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PHYSICAL THERAPY — INITIAL EVALUATION, 12/01/2025
Referral: primary care. Dx: transverse myelitis T5-T7 with lower extremity weakness.

Subjective: discharged from inpatient rehab 11/20. Walking at home with rolling walker. Goal: walk without a device and return to teaching in January.

Objective: Hip flexors 4/5 bilat; knee ext 4+/5; ankle DF/PF 4+/5. Light touch reduced both feet. Gait with rolling walker, slow, reduced step length. Needs arms to rise from a chair.

Assessment: good rehab potential.
Plan: 2x/week for 12 weeks — strengthening, gait and balance training, progression to cane, home program.

documents.title: Neurology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY CLINIC — 12/16/2025

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Hartley returns six weeks after admission for idiopathic acute transverse myelitis (T5-T7; AQP4 and MOG antibodies negative; normal brain MRI; CSF without oligoclonal bands), treated with 5 days of IV methylprednisolone.

She is improving steadily with PT. Walks indoors with a cane now. Bladder function normal. Persistent numbness of both feet. No new symptoms; no vision changes.

Exam: strength 4+/5 throughout both legs. Reduced light touch in both feet. Walks with a cane.

Impression: good ongoing recovery. Nothing to suggest a relapsing disorder at this point; no maintenance therapy indicated.
Plan: continue PT. Repeat MRI thoracic spine with and without contrast in April. Return after the MRI.

Sincerely,
Neurology

documents.title: Back to work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good news — PT and neurology both think I'm ready to go back to my classroom after break. The school needs a note from you saying I can return, with whatever limits you think I need. I'm using the cane in the hallways but not in the room.

documents.title: RE: Back to work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's wonderful. Letter attached and a copy is in your chart: cleared to return to full duties, with a seat available as needed, no recess or bus duty through February, and time off for PT appointments. Ask if they need anything else.

documents.title: Return to Work Letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern:

Christine Hartley is under my care and may return to work as a classroom teacher on January 12, 2026.

Through February 28, 2026, please allow: access to a seat as needed, no outdoor recess or bus duty, and time for twice-weekly physical therapy appointments.

Please contact the office with any questions.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: Prior authorization renewal
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Insulin pen PA for 2026 — insurer auto-renewed Lantus SoloStar; Humalog KwikPen needed a new form, submitted and approved 1/8. Pharmacy confirmed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u myelitis recovery and T1DM.

Back teaching since 1/12. Tired by Friday but managing. Cane only for longer walks and outside on ice. PT twice a week, expects to finish next month. Feet still numb but less so. Bladder normal.

Sugars a little higher this winter — less walking, more grab-and-go food. No lows needing help. No illnesses this winter; flu shot in November.

Vitals as charted. Exam: alert. Heart regular, lungs clear. Legs strong against resistance, slight hip flexor weakness. Light touch reduced over both feet. Gait steady without the cane in the office.

A/P
1. Transverse myelitis — recovering well. Neurology after the April MRI.
2. T1DM — A1c today; expect it a bit up. No dose changes yet; she'd like to see what spring brings once she's walking more.
3. Hashimoto, alopecia areata — stable.
RTC May.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Diabetic eye examination 03/17/2026.
No visual symptoms. BCVA 20/20 OU. Pupils normal. IOP normal.
Dilated fundus OU: no retinopathy, no macular edema. Optic nerves pink and sharp.
Impression: type 1 diabetes, no diabetic retinopathy. Next exam in 12 months.

documents.title: Physical therapy discharge summary
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PHYSICAL THERAPY — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Dates of care: 12/01/2025 - 03/24/2026, 23 visits.
Diagnosis: lower extremity weakness after transverse myelitis T5-T7.

Status at discharge: walking without an assistive device indoors and outdoors, including stairs with a rail. Independent with home exercise program. Residual numbness both feet.

Goals met: independent community ambulation without device; return to work.
Discharged to home program. Re-referral welcome if function declines.

reports.study: MRI thoracic spine with and without contrast
reports.text:
MRI THORACIC SPINE WITHOUT AND WITH IV GADOLINIUM
Indication: follow-up of transverse myelitis T5-T7.
Comparison: 10/29/2025.
Technique: sagittal and axial T1, T2 and STIR; post-contrast T1.
Findings: The intramedullary T2-hyperintense signal at T5-T7 is smaller than on the prior study. No enhancement. No new cord lesions. Alignment and vertebral body heights normal. No disc herniation or stenosis.
reports.conclusion: Interval decrease of the T5-T7 cord signal abnormality. No enhancement and no new lesions.

documents.title: Neurology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY CLINIC — 04/21/2026

Dear Doctor,

Follow-up visit for idiopathic acute transverse myelitis (10/2025), six months out.

She finished PT in March and walks without any device. Teaching full time. Mild numbness remains in both feet. Bladder and bowel normal. No new neurologic symptoms in the interval.

Exam: strength 5/5 in both legs except hip flexors 5-/5 bilaterally. Mildly reduced light touch in both feet. Gait normal.

MRI thoracic spine 4/14/2026: T5-T7 signal smaller, no enhancement, no new lesions.

Impression: monophasic idiopathic transverse myelitis with near-complete recovery. No further treatment needed.
Plan: return to neurology in 6 months, sooner for any new weakness, sensory change, vision loss or bladder symptoms.

Sincerely,
Neurology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
T1DM visit. Walking again in the evenings since April, and her afternoon sugars show it. Fasting 110-140. No lows below 60.

Neurology letter from April reviewed — near-complete recovery, no treatment, follow-up in the fall.

Vitals as charted. Exam: well. Gait normal. Feet: skin intact, pulses normal; light touch mildly reduced both feet.

Plan: A1c today. No insulin changes. Physical in August.

documents.title: Refill — levothyroxine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill request levothyroxine 88 mcg 90-day. TSH 8/2025 normal. Sent with 1 refill; TSH due with August physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 35 last month. A good summer — back to hiking, short trails. No illnesses, no hospital visits this year. Feet still a bit numb at the toes, otherwise she feels back to herself. Starting the school year next week.

Meds: insulin glargine 18 u qHS; insulin lispro 1:12 + correction; levothyroxine 88 mcg daily. NKDA.
Problems: T1DM; Hashimoto hypothyroidism; alopecia areata (in remission); DKA 2/2025 (resolved); idiopathic transverse myelitis 10/2025 (recovered, neurology following).
FH: mother Hashimoto's; father T2DM; maternal aunt RA; sister celiac.
SH: teacher; lives with a roommate; never smoker; 1-2 drinks a month.

ROS: no weakness, no bladder change, no vision change. Otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Scalp: hair full, no patches of alopecia. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Neuro: strength full except slight hip flexor weakness, gait normal. Feet: skin intact, no calluses, pulses 2+, light touch mildly reduced over the toes, monofilament felt at all sites.

PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
- T1DM: A1c, CMP, urine albumin/creatinine, lipids. No changes. Sick-day plan refreshed before school.
- Hashimoto: TSH.
- Transverse myelitis: recovered; neurology in October.
- Alopecia areata: in remission since 1/2025.
- Flu vaccine this fall. Pap/HPV due 2029.
RTC November.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your physical labs are back and look good: A1c a little better than in May, thyroid normal, kidneys and urine protein normal, cholesterol fine. Have a great first week with the new class. See you in November.
